headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors from Pipecat’s shared-bus, multi-API voice pipeline into Taipy workflows; data leakage is limited by Taipy’s no-egress profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pipecat can ingest and emit text, audio, images, and conversation state over a shared bus, so attacker-controlled content can reach downstream consumers. Taipy has no documented ingestion channel, but if it consumes Pipecat outputs as instructions, prompt injection is plausible. The pairwise pathway is inferred from Pipecat’s shared-state design and Taipy’s automation role.
conditions: IF Taipy reads Pipecat-generated text from the shared bus or files as instructions, injection risk is active.
IF Pipecat outputs are manually reviewed before Taipy consumes them, this pathway is reduced.
mitigations: Add a strict schema/allowlist for any Pipecat-to-Taipy text handoff.
Insert a human review step before Taipy executes Pipecat-derived instructions.
Strip markup, tool directives, and code fences from Pipecat outputs.
Use separate buses or queues for raw content and executable commands.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and rejection rules in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pipecat touches audio, video, images, text, and conversation state and can egress to allowlisted third-party APIs, so sensitive content may leave its boundary. Taipy’s profile shows no network egress and no data classes touched, so it is not a likely exfiltration sink. The pairwise leakage risk is therefore limited and depends on shared workspace or explicit forwarding.
conditions: IF Pipecat and Taipy share a workspace containing sensitive transcripts or media, leakage risk increases.
IF Taipy is configured to forward Pipecat artifacts to external services, the risk changes materially.
mitigations: Keep Pipecat and Taipy on separate workspaces.
Disable or restrict Pipecat connectors that send content to third parties.
Store only redacted transcripts in any shared directory.
Audit shared folders for audio/video/text artifacts before runs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pipecat supports shared-bus, multi-instance operation and can write or coordinate across processes, while Taipy is a data-engineering framework with no documented write or network surfaces here. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable-resource writes, so direct conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because Taipy’s write surfaces are undocumented, so I choose the lower but nonzero severity.
conditions: IF Taipy writes to the same files, database, or job state as Pipecat, conflict risk becomes active.
IF the orchestrator provides locking, this conflict is reduced.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories to each agent.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same database or git branch.
Run one agent at a time for shared resources.
Add file locks around any shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: implement transactional coordination for shared mutable state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat can generate conversational text and analytics that Taipy could plausibly consume in automation or scheduling workflows. Taipy’s data-engineering role makes downstream action-taking plausible, so if it treats Pipecat output as authoritative, errors can cascade into multiple work products. The interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes the severity upward from low.
conditions: IF Taipy uses Pipecat output as an input to scheduled jobs or automated decisions, cascading error risk is active.
IF Taipy verifies Pipecat outputs against independent sources, the risk is reduced.
mitigations: Require validation before Taipy acts on Pipecat output.
Log and diff Pipecat outputs against source data.
Use confidence thresholds before automation triggers.
Route Pipecat output to a staging table first.
requires-engineering: add end-to-end provenance and verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Pipecat’s docs-only profile shows it can handle audio, video, images, text, and conversation state and may send data to third-party APIs; Taipy shows no egress and no touched data classes. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to whatever sensitive data Pipecat processes. I do not cite Taipy-specific compliance gaps because none are present in the profile.
conditions: IF Pipecat processes regulated data and sends it to a non-approved external API, compliance risk increases.
IF the deployment keeps regulated data out of Pipecat, this risk is reduced.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to Pipecat.
Disable external API connectors for regulated workloads.
Keep regulated transcripts out of shared storage.
Review vendor terms for each Pipecat API provider.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls per connector.
